description: Inspect the characters a CSV actually contains before it is imported: a UTF-8 byte-order mark, mixed CRLF and LF line endings, NUL bytes, undecodable replacement characters, control characters, mojibake and non-ASCII column names, each with the evidence that identifies it. Choose this when a CSV imports with a broken first column name, fails on accented text, or shows a row count you did not expect, and you want the character-level reason rather than a row-level report. Do not choose this when the rows need checking for shape or types (use csv-preflight or csv-type-coercion-check), or when a UTF-16 file should be converted rather than diagnosed. Example requests: Why does my CSV have a column called '﻿id' instead of 'id'? | Are the line endings in this CSV consistent? | Check this CSV for encoding problems before I import it.

accepted_price.description: The quoted amount, echoed exactly; checked against the quote.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

buyer_token.description: The buyer_token returned with your first purchase. It opens the purchase history for that buyer, including earlier deliverables.

idempotency_key.description: Retry key; the same key returns the same job.

content.description: The customer's input.csv, as text. Supported: CSV, TSV or any delimiter-separated text. Maximum 1048576 bytes.
